oneOf.description: HTTP call. URL, method, headers and body are all expressions, so the whole request can be driven from the context.

items.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

accepted_status.description: HTTP status patterns accepted as non-errors, e.g. "2xx" or "404" (defaults to any 2xx). Author it as a literal array (each element a ${ } template or $: expression yielding a string), or as a single $: expression yielding the whole array.

body.description: Templated value building the request body; an object is sent as JSON. Of self, only self.previous is in scope — the action has not run yet.

additionalProperties.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

headers.description: Request headers, evaluating to an object of string values. Author it as a literal map (each value a ${ } template or a $: expression yielding a string), or as a single $: expression yielding the whole map.

method.description: HTTP method, a template (e.g. GET, POST, ${ input.method }). Defaults to POST.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

items.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

anyOf.description: A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.
A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.
A literal string, or a $: expression / ${ } template evaluated against the context.

query.description: Query parameters appended to the url, evaluating to an object of scalar values. A null value omits its parameter. Author it as a literal map (each value a ${ } template or a $: expression) or as a single $: expression yielding the whole map.

responses.description: Status pattern -> JSON Schema for that status's body. Keys are exact codes or hundred-ranges ("200", "400, 401", "5xx"). A 2xx key types self.result and accepts the status; a non-2xx key types error.data.

url.description: Request URL. May contain ${ } interpolations evaluated against the current context (e.g. ${ config.server_url }/path).

oneOf.description: Single child-process call: runs one named process and waits. The result is the child's output directly, as outputs.taskID.

input.description: Templated value building the child's input payload. Of self, only self.previous is in scope — the action has not run yet.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, readable as error.data in a rule that catches it. null declares a code carrying no data; omitting one leaves error.data absent.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing the child's output. Without it the output is only self.result, in this task's switch.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

oneOf.description: Keyed child-process call: runs named processes concurrently and waits for all. The result is keyed by child name, as outputs.taskID.childKey.

input.description: Templated value building the child's input payload. Of self, only self.previous is in scope — the action has not run yet.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, per entry since entries can be different processes. Readable as error.data in a rule that catches it.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing this child's output; declaring a shape narrows what the child left untyped.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

children.description: Keyed map of child processes to run concurrently. Keys become the access names in outputs.taskID.

oneOf.description: List fan-out: one child per element of 'over', run concurrently. The result is an array of their outputs in 'over' order, as outputs.taskID.

name.description: Name of the child process to invoke for every element.

over.description: A $: expression evaluating to an array; one child is spawned per element, with that element as its input. An empty array yields an empty result.

raises.description: Raise code -> JSON Schema for that code's payload, readable as error.data in a rule that catches it. null declares a code carrying no data; omitting one leaves error.data absent.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema validating and exposing EACH child's output; the collected result is an array of values conforming to it.

version.description: Version to run; 0 means latest published version.

oneOf.description: Delay action: parks the instance until a duration elapses (for) or an instant arrives (until), holding no worker. Exactly one of for / until.

for.description: A duration from when the task is reached: a literal such as "2h30m" (units ms, s, m, h, d, w, mo, y), a bare number of milliseconds, or a $: expression yielding milliseconds.

tz.description: IANA name ("Europe/Prague") or fixed offset ("+02:00") for calendar units and wall clocks; defaults to UTC. Abbreviations like "CET" are rejected as ambiguous across DST.

until.description: An instant: RFC 3339, "2026-09-01 08:00", "+2d 08:00", a calendar or clock pattern ("mon 09:00", "*:*:00"), unix milliseconds, or a $: expression. A past instant resolves immediately.

oneOf.description: External task: parks the instance until an outside caller submits a result, holding no worker. An absent timeout waits forever; a timeout raises the catchable external.timeout.

input.description: Templated value snapshotted for the resolver — the only context the queue exposes. Of self, only self.previous is in scope.

raises.description: Code -> JSON Schema for the payload a worker submits to /external-tasks/fail, readable as error.data in a rule that catches it. An undeclared code is still accepted.

result_schema.description: JSON Schema the submitted result is validated against before the instance resumes. Without it any JSON result is accepted, available as self.result.

case.description: Boolean expression checked in ADDITION to code — the same predicate a switch case is, on the error channel. A false case falls through to the next rule, and an error every rule declines is unmatched.

code.description: Patterns matched against the error code. '%' is the only wildcard; every other character, '_' and '.' included, is literal. Empty list = catch-all. On a child task they match what the child can raise, plus output.invalid.

goto.description: Task to route to when retries are exhausted. '$task-id' or 'end'. Omit to fail the instance.

not_reached.description: Assert this code means the remote was never reached, allowing retries on only_once tasks. Omit to use the engine's default (pre.* = not reached).

panic.description: Terminate as 'failed' with this code and message instead of routing — a defect. Nothing catches a panic. Exclusive with goto and raise.

raise.description: Terminate as 'raised' with this code and message instead of routing — an anticipated condition a parent can catch. Exclusive with goto and panic.

retry.description: Retry policy applied before the rule routes: a bare attempt count, or an object naming attempts / delay / factor / max_delay. Omit for no retries.

code.description: Error code, lower_snake_case, no dots (dots are reserved for engine-produced codes). A literal — never an expression.

data.description: Structured payload this fault carries, evaluated when the clause fires. It lands on error.data, which an operator reads on the instance detail and in logs.

message.description: Human-readable message. A template: ${ } interpolations render when the clause fires and must produce a non-null string.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for 'attempts': the number of retries before following goto or failing, on the default backoff curve (1s, doubling, capped at 5m).
The long form, naming the attempt count and any part of the backoff curve. Every slot also accepts a $: expression, so a policy can be driven from config.

attempts.description: Number of retries before following goto or failing. 0 = no retries. A $: expression must evaluate to a whole number.

delay.description: Wait before the first retry: a duration such as "30s" (units ms, s, m, h only — the curve scales this), a bare number of milliseconds, or a $: expression. Defaults to 1s.

factor.description: Multiplier applied to the wait after each further attempt. 1 keeps the delay constant. A $: expression must evaluate to a number of at least 1. Defaults to 2.

max_delay.description: Ceiling the growing wait is clamped to, in the same grammar as 'delay'. Defaults to 5m, or to 'delay' when that is longer. Must not be shorter than 'delay'.

anyOf.description: A $: typed expression, a ${ } interpolation template, or a literal string.
Literal array; each element is recursively a Shape.
Literal object; each value is recursively a Shape.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for a single unconditional route: "next" (not valid on the last task), "end", or "$task-id".
Ordered routing rules; first match wins and the last entry must be a catch-all (omit 'case'). Each case sets exactly one of 'goto', 'raise' or 'panic'.

case.description: Boolean expression. Omit for a catch-all; must be last.

goto.description: "end" to terminate, "next" to advance, or "$task-id" to jump to a task.

panic.description: Terminate as 'failed' with this code and message — a defect. Nothing can catch a panic; the code exists to classify the failure, not to branch on it.

raise.description: Terminate as 'raised' with this code and message — an anticipated condition a parent process may react to by naming the code in its on_error.

action.description: Describes the action to perform. Omit for switch-only (routing) tasks.

id.description: Task identifier, unique within the definition.

on_error.description: Ordered error-routing rules evaluated when the call fails. First match wins.

only_once.description: At-most-once execution: retries are allowed only for pre.* errors or rules with not_reached:true, and never where nothing came back. A crash raises the catchable only_once.interrupted. Defaults to false.

output.description: Templated value remapping this task's output, evaluated with self.result and self.previous in scope. When set it is what outputs.taskID holds and the switch sees as self.output.

switch.description: Required. Routing: a scalar shorthand ("next", "end", "$task-id") or an ordered list of cases whose last entry is a catch-all.

timeout.description: Maximum execution time for fetch and external tasks: a duration shorthand, or an object naming one of 'for' / 'until' plus 'tz'. 'until' is external-only. Omit for the engine default.

oneOf.description: Shorthand for 'for', resolved in UTC: a duration such as "2h30m", a bare number of milliseconds, or a $: expression yielding milliseconds.
The long form, naming exactly one of 'for' or 'until' plus an optional 'tz'.

for.description: A duration from when the task is reached, e.g. "2h30m", a bare number of milliseconds, or a $: expression.

tz.description: IANA name ("Europe/Prague") or fixed offset ("+02:00") for calendar units and wall clocks; defaults to UTC. Abbreviations like "CET" are rejected as ambiguous across DST.

until.description: An absolute deadline, external tasks only. Accepts the same instants as a delay's 'until': RFC 3339, a calendar pattern, unix milliseconds, or a $: expression.

additionalProperties.description: A JSON Schema, in the subset genroc supports.

$anchor.description: A name this schema can be referenced by.

$defs.description: Named schemas this document's $refs resolve against.

$ref.description: A reference to another schema, as `#/$defs/<name>`.

additionalProperties.description: The schema undeclared keys conform to, making the object an open map. Omit to close the object: undeclared keys are stripped.

anyOf.description: The value conforms to at least one of these schemas.

default.description: The value used when this one is absent. Annotation only — it does not make a required property optional.

description.description: Free text. Shown in the editor, and never a constraint.

enum.description: The complete set of values allowed here.

items.description: The schema every element of an array conforms to.

oneOf.description: The value conforms to exactly one of these schemas.

properties.description: The named members of an object, each a schema.

required.description: Which properties must be present. A property not listed here may be absent, and reading it yields null.

secret.description: Redacts the value from logs. Only meaningful in a process config_schema.

type.description: The value's JSON type, or a list of types it may take.

$defs.description: Shared schema definitions referenced as "#/$defs/<name>", which may reference each other. A name colliding with a generated one is kept but renamed with a suffix.

config_schema.description: JSON Schema — a flat object of primitive properties — declaring config variables, each resolved from GENROC_<PROCESS>_<NAME> (or GENROC_GLOBAL_<NAME>) and exposed as config.<NAME>. secret:true redacts it from logs.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema used to validate the input payload when starting a new instance.

output.description: Templated value (a string expression or nested object of expressions) evaluated at completion to produce the process output.

tasks.description: Ordered list of execution tasks. Control advances linearly unless a switch case redirects.
